subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-month-old girl is evaluated because of episodes of vomiting and irritability that began at 10 days of life. Newborn screening showed elevated leucine, and she has been managed with a formula restricted in branched-chain amino acids. Genetic testing shows a partial defect of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex. Her metabolic team recommends a trial of a vitamin supplement that serves as a cofactor for this enzyme complex, in addition to continuing her diet.
question: Which of the following vitamins is most likely to be supplemented in this patient?
explanation_correct: The branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex is a multienzyme dehydrogenase complex homologous to pyruvate dehydrogenase and alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and all three require thiamine pyrophosphate. Thiamine supplementation can improve residual enzyme activity in patients with an intermediate or thiamine-responsive form of maple syrup urine disease, whereas dietary restriction of leucine, isoleucine, and valine remains the mainstay of treatment.

explanation_incorrect.A: Biotin is the cofactor for carboxylation reactions such as pyruvate carboxylase, acetyl-CoA carboxylase, and propionyl-CoA carboxylase, not for alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complexes.
explanation_incorrect.B: Cobalamin is a cofactor for methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase and has no role in branched-chain amino acid catabolism.
explanation_incorrect.C: Pyridoxal phosphate is the cofactor for transamination and decarboxylation reactions; the transamination step of branched-chain amino acid catabolism is B6-dependent, but the dehydrogenase that is deficient in maple syrup urine disease is not.
explanation_incorrect.E: Tetrahydrofolate carries one-carbon units in nucleotide and methionine metabolism and is not a cofactor of the branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase complex.

educationalObjective: Branched-chain alpha-ketoacid dehydrogenase is a thiamine pyrophosphate-dependent complex, so thiamine supplementation may benefit thiamine-responsive forms of maple syrup urine disease.
